messages.subject: how to deal with very large data
parts:
Hi All,

I have some problem about dealing with large biological data.  I am planning to plot a box plot for my data, but my data is extremely large, the excel column is 20687 for each, and I have 11 teams, I need to plot them together for comparison.  Does anybody have the experience of dealing with such large data?

Thanks,

Chen

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: how to deal with very large data
parts:
Hi:

As Sean mentioned, if you have 20K observations for each of 11
variables, this is no big deal if you have sufficient RAM. Here's a
reproducible example to show how it could be done in "proof of
concept" fashion.

# Generate a 22K x 11 matrix, name the columns V1-V11
m <- matrix(rnorm(242000), ncol = 11, dimnames = list(NULL,
paste0("V", seq(11))))

library(reshape2)

# Use the melt() function to convert the matrix into
# a data frame in long form. Var1 = row numbers,
# Var2 = variable names
DFm <- melt(DF)
str(DFm) # interested in Var2 and value

library(ggplot2)

# boxplots for V1-V11
ggplot(DFm, aes(x = Var2, y = value) + geom_boxplot()

# Boxplots inside violin plots - a violin plot provides a
# density estimate
# Since the simulated data is N(0, 1), each violin plot should
# look like a normal density on each side of the center.
ggplot(DFm, aes(x = Var2, y = value)) +
geom_violin(fill = "orange", alpha = 0.2) +
geom_boxplot(fill = "blue", alpha = 0.1)

Dennis
